Chinese food in the restaurant area of the Takashimaya building
Dec 2023 • Solo
I thought the whole building was Takashimaya, but it's not all of it, I found out later.

I recommend this restaurant area because it's air-conditioned even in the heat and the toilets are clean.

I went in because I wanted to eat mapo tofu.

You are given a tablet to order from. It has pictures, so it's easy to use.

However, the menu is in Vietnamese, so I just tapped randomly to order. Each dish has an English description and price.

I looked for rice but couldn't find it, so I asked the waiter in English, but he didn't understand until the third person finally understood and gave me rice on the tablet.

Mapo tofu, rice, two beers, and beans as an appetizer (which seems to come automatically) cost about 2,200 yen.

The mapo tofu was delicious.

It seems that this restaurant is a chain with its main store in Singapore.

When you order beer (can or bottle) in Vietnam, you get a glass, but be careful because it always comes with ice. I got it in an open bowl at this restaurant.
Ice is provided, but the beer itself is kept nice and cold at every bar. English is generally not spoken, so it's a good idea to learn how to say "no ice" in Vietnamese.

I’ve heard of the crystal jade - they’re mostly in Asia and I know that one of their branches earned 1 Michelin Star. So we went ahead and tried their food -ordered fried mango shrimp I think and that was delicious. Ordered their signature fried rice - that was ok and it’s not that too oily. There are some other better choices
Sep 2018 • Friends
The restaurant is located in Takashimaya mall, right in the center of the city.
As a party of 4, we ordered 2 dim sum choices as starters and the famous Peking duck prepared 3 ways: rolls of crispy skin, meat sautéed with vegetables and deep fried bones.
The overall quality of the food was just average, a bit too greasy. Watch out for the quantity, you get to be very hungry to finish the duck dishes.
The young waiters were nice, polite, but unprofessional: orders had to be repeated several times, beers were served in cans without glasses...
Price was reasonable but on the high side compared to other local Chinese restaurants.

For Cantonese in D1, this place delivers consistently.

Food is excellent - we like the Peking Duck served two ways, the traditional dim sum dishes, and the fried shrimp with salted egg coating as a light batter.

Last time we had two friends who are vegetarians, so I was worried about bringing them to dim sum. But they enjoyed themselves with an assortment of veggie dishes like the "Braised Spinach Tofu with Assorted Mushrooms" and "Braised Tofu with Mushroom and Vegetables" so I took a picture to make sure I have the correct name of the dishes.
